breakdown.description: The given relative velocities/angles imply different axial components, contradicting the statement that axial velocity is constant.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve the physical inconsistency. It calculated the axial velocity from the inlet conditions (Va = 106.1 m/s) but then proceeded to use the original, inconsistent outlet relative velocity (W2 = 100 m/s) in its calculations. This value of W2 implies an outlet axial velocity of 86.6 m/s (100 * cos(30)), which contradicts the problem's constraint that axial velocity is constant. The ground truth correctly identifies this and recalculates W2 to be consistent with the inlet axial velocity, a crucial step the agent missed.
